A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Hyper-Connections and contain readable main text and Appendices A–L. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the equations, figures, tables, and rotated appendix tables without material gaps.

before.justification: v2 reports original language-model training, downstream evaluations, ablations, and ImageNet generation and classification experiments in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds measured memory footprints in Table 9 and a parallel-transformer-block training comparison in Figure 18.

M1.justification: The static and dynamic hyper-connection equations, initialization, and Algorithms 1–3 are unchanged. Corrections to connection labels in Figures 2 and 8 do not change the specified architecture or procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same language-model training corpora, validation and downstream tasks, and ImageNet generation and classification tasks. The added memory measurements and PTB comparison do not introduce different data or task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 Figure 18 adds OLMo-1B-PTB as a training-loss comparator against OLMo-1B and DHC×4 variants. v2 discusses and visualizes parallel transformer blocks but lacks this performance comparison. Existing comparisons with Altup, ResiDual, and other baselines are retained.

E3.justification: New Table 9 introduces empirical memory evaluation in GB and percentage overhead on eight GPUs, with matched microbatch sizes within each model family. Existing language and vision evaluation protocols remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish revisions to their training settings.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds measurements testing how actual memory overhead varies with expansion rate and model family, extending v2's analytical treatment. Existing expansion-rate, tanh, static-versus-dynamic, frozen-component, and connection-pattern analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed-based uncertainty, or significance tests for performance comparisons. Figure 3's median and 5th–95th percentile display is unchanged, and the added results introduce no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: New Table 9 reports memory measurements, including 26.27 GB for OLMo-7B versus 33.70 GB for DHC×4, a reported 28.28% overhead. New Figure 18 shows PTB finishing with higher training loss than the baseline and DHC×4 variants. Existing numerical results, including the renumbered appendix tables, are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, connection-matrix derivations, complexity formulas, and residual-equivalence and sequential-parallel arguments remain unchanged, including Appendices B and F–H. Diagram-label corrections do not revise these formal results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about replacing residual connections, learning connection strengths and layer arrangements, and improving language and vision models. The additions supply evidence without changing the scope of these claims.

C2.justification: The interpretations of learned connection patterns, failure at expansion rate one, and diminishing benefits during repeated ImageNet training are retained. Appendix B adds memory measurements without substantively revising its qualitative memory discussion or limitations.

D1.justification: Table 9 newly specifies eight GPUs and microbatch sizes of 16,384, 2,048, and 4,096 tokens per GPU for the 1B dense, 7B dense, and MoE memory measurements, respectively. Existing implementation code, initialization details, and training hyperparameters are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work discussion, and novelty positioning are unchanged. PTB and its Wang (2021) citation already appear in v2; its added experimental comparison introduces no new citation or substantive positioning statement.

P1.justification: The header changes from 'Preprint' to 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2025', Figure 3's caption receives a small wording edit, and Appendix B gains a sentence introducing measurements. Section order and the overall narrative are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds memory Table 9 and PTB Figure 18, corrects duplicated connection-weight indices in Figures 2 and 8, and adjusts Figure 3's placement and text wrapping. Subsequent tables are renumbered and some content reflows, without a substantial visual redesign.

improvement.justification: Measured memory overhead in Table 9 makes resource tradeoffs more concrete than v2's analytical discussion alone, and Figure 18 fills a limited performance-comparison gap for PTB. Corrected diagram labels also improve consistency. These are useful incremental gains; the core results and theory remain unchanged, and the memory-measurement procedure remains sparsely documented.
